cells.formattedValue: The 2026 private-pilot training scholarship is for applicants age 16–23 at the deadline who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents, do not already hold a private pilot certificate, meet the foundation's stated conduct and FAA English requirements, and can train during May–December 2026. University-based flight-program students are excluded. Passing the written exam or obtaining authorization to take it was required before May 15, 2026; medical/IACRA requirements apply before accepting training. Two recommendations must be received by the application deadline, with three original essay responses. The 2026 application closed January 31; the posted annual window is October 31–January 31, without a newly verified next-cycle application.

cells.formattedValue: This is an automatic, merit-based scholarship for Montana freshmen demonstrating academic promise based on their cumulative high school GPA. Award amounts vary based on GPA, ranging from $1,000 to $4,000 per year, and are renewable for four years for tuition only. Students are automatically considered upon submitting an application for admission with a self-reported GPA. For the published fall 2026 award, renewal requires a cumulative college GPA of at least 2.5, at least 15 credits each semester, continued Montana residency and continuous enrollment. This is for a first undergraduate bachelor’s degree. Fall 2027 scholarship terms are not yet available.

cells.formattedValue: UM Academic Achievement Scholarship (UMAAS) is an admission-based tuition award for out-of-state new undergraduates and transfers pursuing their first bachelor's degree; international undergraduates may qualify. It is not a promise to cover all tuition. The program-specific page lists March 1 without a cycle year. Renewal requires 2.5 cumulative GPA and enrollment/credit progress, with different pre/post-fall-2025 terms. The page conflicts about whether gaining Montana residency forfeits renewal and uses both semester and annual-credit formulations; confirm those points before relying on renewal. Initial Montana-resident applicants are directed to other scholarships.

cells.formattedValue: The current Carroll Pell Promise page describes fall 2027 first-time freshmen and transfer students residing in the U.S., living on campus, qualifying for Pell through FAFSA, maintaining a 3.0 GPA and completing at least 12 credits per semester, for up to eight semesters. Tuition support combines federal aid, Carroll merit/need gift aid and subsidized Stafford borrowing; it is not all grant funding or a guarantee of full tuition. The introductory steps say to agree to borrow $3,500, while detailed criteria assume maximum subsidized loans of $3,500/$4,500/$5,500 by year; this wording difference remains unresolved. Summer/winter tuition, study abroad and fees are excluded; additional criteria and athletic-aid exceptions may apply. These current 2027 terms differ from the unavailable historical Montana-only 2026 page.

cells.formattedValue: Black Mountain Software will be awarding two $1,000.00 scholarships to graduating seniors in Montana. Any Montana high school senior graduating in 2026 may apply if he or she will be attending an accredited institution of higher education. These accredited institutions include trade schools, technical schools, colleges or universities. The applicant’s field of study may be any field that they want to pursue. Applications and essays must be submitted electronically to Black Mountain Software. Please see the scholarship application for instructions for completing the application form and requirements for the essay. All submissions must be received before midnight on or before February 26th, 2026. Essay Question: If you were given a team of developers to build one new piece of software (an app, a program, a game) that would make the world a more joyful, curious, or connected place, what would it be and why? Describe its core function and the problem it solves for its users. The essay is limited to 2000 characters (300-350 words) or less.

cells.formattedValue: This scholarship is available to any Whitefish High School senior who is entering a four year university with plans to major in an environmental science field. Eligible majors include; environmental science/studies, environmental engineering, biology, and sustainability. Other majors will be considered if they demonstrate a link to an environmental emphasis. A brief essay also needs to be included (300-500 words) describing your “watershed ethic.” In short, what is your philosophy regarding human activities that affect water quality in the Whitefish Lake Watershed? How does your watershed ethic make you a good steward of water resources in the Whitefish Lake Watershed? Paper applications to be mailed to: Whitefish Lake Institute, Ripple Effect Applications 550 E. 1st St. #103 Whitefish, MT 59937 or emailed to: Info@whitefishlake.org // Subject: Ripple Effect Application

cells.formattedValue: All entries must start with the local VFW post. Contact the Whitefish VFW to see about participating. Record your original 3-5 minute (+ or – 5 second max.) audio essay on a flash drive, or other electronic device. Hearing/speech impaired students should email the Voice of Democracy National Office at youth scholarships@vfw.org for special instructions. No music, singing, poetry or sound effects are allowed. The body of the essay must not identify you in any way, (including, but not limited to your name, school, city, state, race, or national origin) although the recording & typed essay should be labeled with your name, to show ownership. All entries competing at the local Post level must be in the hands of that VFW Post by midnight, Oct. 31, 2025.  Originality is worth 35 points (treatment of the theme should show imagination and human interest), Content is worth 30 points (clearly express your ideas in an organized manner. Fully develop your theme and use transitions to move smoothly from one idea to another), Delivery is worth 35 points (speak in a clear and credible manner). Read application for further details. You will submit the recording, typed essay and this completed entry form to: Dustin Wegner, Commander     20 Baker Ave., Whitefish, MT  59937 (you can mail or drop off in person). Call Dustin Wegner with questions: 406.654.4020

cells.formattedValue: The Hagan Scholarship is a nationwide need-based merit scholarship, designed to provide recipients with the opportunity to graduate college debt-free. Applicants must attend a traditional public high school governed by a school district. Free workshops, Free Schwab Brokerage Accounts and Free Study Abroad provide recipients with a practical understanding of important life skills not typically covered in the school curriculum. (Hagan Scholarship Brochure). Applicant’s Adjusted Gross Household Income reported for 2023 Federal Income Tax Purposes must not have exceeded $100,000. “Household Income” is defined as the total income received by all members of a household living under the same roof. Applicants must show evidence they will be working 240 hours from January 1, 2026 to September 1, 2026 (they understand that most recipients work during the summer months. Work can be part-time during their senior year in high school or full-time during the summer or a combination of the two. They are looking for "students willing to contribute toward their educational expenses."

No new open cycle is inferred.

cells.formattedValue: The Dennis & Phyllis Washington Foundation's Horatio Alger Montana Undergraduate Scholarship provides up to $15,000 over four years for students who have overcome adversity. Its detailed eligibility still specifies full-time Montana high-school seniors graduating in spring/summer 2026, entering the Montana University System no later than the following fall, US citizenship, critical financial need, integrity/perseverance and co-curricular, after-school or community activity involvement. Pell-eligible families are encouraged; Pell eligibility is not stated as mandatory. Recipients must pursue and complete a bachelor's degree but may start at a two-year institution and transfer. Eligible institutions include UM, MSU and the named Montana affiliates. The page gives December 1–February 15 for seniors and December 1–March 1 for juniors; junior eligibility details and the next cycle year are not fully stated. Apply through Horatio Alger; an existing National Scholarship application is automatically considered. Recipients maintain a 2.0 GPA to keep the award; this is a renewal condition, not a verified entrance minimum. The current page does not substantiate the older $10,000 plus $5,000 split.

cells.formattedValue:
JUST FOR WHITEFISH STUDENTS!!! The Kiita Foundation Scholarship (Kiita rhymes with cheetah) was established in 2023 by Jim and Jo-Ann Armstrong. They want to help a high achieving, financially independent student achieve a bachelor's degree. By financially independent, we mean someone who cannot rely on their family to help pay for college.  This award is very generous... up to $10,000 per year and renewable for up to 4 years. The recipient also has the opportunity to participate in all-expense paid service learning trips to Mexico with a cohort of other students.  They are looking for someone who is highly engaged in school and community activities. Again, they need to be financially independent when it comes to paying for college.  
The following essay questions: 1) This scholarship is for students who cannot rely on their family to help pay for college. Please explain why you need the assistance of this scholarship. 2) Please describe any obstacles in your path to high school graduation and how you have overcome them. 3) Please describe why you are interested in pursuing a bachelor’s degree and what you believe you are capable of achieving once you have earned your degree. You may explain this in terms of your life goals, career goals, and/or goals within your community. 4) Describe volunteer activities in which you have chosen to participate, why you chose those particular volunteer activities, and how those experiences have affected your life. Please contact Jill Seigmund at Whitefish Community Foundation with questions: (406) 863-1781 or jill@whitefishcommunityfoundation.org

cells.formattedValue: The Big Sky State Games has teamed up with the CHARACTER COUNTS! Coalition and Mountain Alarm Fire and Security to recognize the importance of sportsmanship and character in Montana student athletes. CHARACTER COUNTS! is a nonprofit organization striving to improve the character of today’s youth. It is based on common ethical values that transcend political, religious, socio-economic, and cultural differences. Called the “Six Pillars of Character,” these values are: trustworthiness, respect, responsibility, fairness, caring and citizenship. Character Counts! Scholarship is sponsored by Mountain Alarm Fire and Security. Over the past twenty-four years, the Big Sky State Games has awarded the Character Counts! Scholarship to outstanding Montana female and male student-citizen-athletes involved in the Big Sky State Games. The scholarship can be used for any secondary education after high school. This includes trade schools and community colleges. Only high school juniors during the 2025-2026 school year are eligible for this scholarship. This is to ensure that fellow students can observe the scholarship winners during their senior year and to recognize the traits the students show. You can fill out the application below. It will also be available at all Montana High Schools Guidance Counselor offices.

cells.formattedValue: Diversity Scholarship Application; expand the perspectives shared and voices heard. Preference to underrepresented groups. Essay topic of 300 words: "What is the importance of diversity and inclusion?"  Water & Environmental Technologies, Inc. (WET) is a technical environmental and engineering consulting firm committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace. We believe innovation and creativity come when companies advocate for a varied range of experience, talent, and ideas. To continue our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, we are offering a scholarship for first year college students who share our passion and vision to expand the perspectives shared and voices heard. WET will award two (2) $1,000 scholarships. This scholarship is open to Montana and Wyoming High School students, but preference will be given to those who are members of an underrepresented class* (i.e. include, but are not limited to, the following: ethnicity, disability, gender, sexual orientation, income, education, etc.) Paper Application and all required attachments should be submitted to: WATER & ENVIRONMENTAL TECHNOLOGIES   ATTENTION: DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION COMMITTEE   480 EAST PARK STREET    BUTTE, MT 59701  or Applications can also be submitted on our website at the following link:  waterenvtech.com/diversityscholarship

cells.formattedValue: Open to MANRRS members and their children. High school seniors, college students or nontraditional students seeking funding to attend a two or four-year accredited college or university or technical school for any area of study may apply. Application Deadline: April 1, 2026. Recipients will be selected and announced by July 31, 2026.

cells.formattedValue: Scholarship awards $2,500 to high-achieving young women who are in their final year of high school and plan to attend an accredited postsecondary educational institution in the US or Canada in the next academic year. LEADERSHIP, ACADEMICS, EXTRACURRICULAR ACTIVITIES, COMMUNITY SERVICE and potential for future success are key attributes. There are 2 Whitefish chapters and each can nominate one outstanding young woman for consideration. To apply, the process needs to start THIS YEAR via interested JUNIOR GRADE women should send an electronic copy of their resume to either Chapter BR (peomtchapterbr@gmail.com) or Chapter D (PEOchapterD.MT@gmail.com) no later than May 15. After review of resumes, each local chapter will conduct brief interviews to determine a nominee who will, in turn, complete an online application to P.E.O. International for final consideration. The online application process can start as early as August 15 but no later than October 15. Nominees are notified of the outcome in mid-April of their senior year.

cells.formattedValue: MSU Hilleman Scholars is a program for Montana residents who are recent Montana high-school graduates with academic, leadership and career potential. The official application is labeled Fall 2026 without an exact deadline; the details page describes selection by invitation and still contains a 2025 orientation date. The program offers $4,000 per year for four years, conditional on academic progress and 10–15 hours each week of mentoring, learning, internship and community development activities. Completion of the Summer Success Academy is required to retain the offer, with a separate $2,000 academy stipend. The stated group study-abroad support is conditional. Hilleman cannot be stacked with Horatio Alger funding. Neither Pell eligibility nor first-generation status is established as a mandatory requirement by the checked public rules.

cells.formattedValue: Soroptimist Live Your Dream Awards are for women who provide primary financial support for themselves and their dependents and have financial need. Applicants must be enrolled in or accepted to a vocational/skills training or undergraduate degree program and be motivated to achieve their education and career goals. High-school-equivalency study alone is not listed as an eligible program. Dependents may include children, spouse, partner, siblings or parents. Applicants must reside in a Soroptimist International of the Americas member country or territory, including the United States; previous Women's Opportunity or Live Your Dream recipients, people with or pursuing a graduate degree, Soroptimist members, employees and their immediate family are ineligible. Applications run August 1–November 15 (cycle year not stated). Club awards vary; selected recipients may progress to regional and international levels, for a potential total of $1,000–$16,000. Written sections must reflect the applicant's own experiences and goals; AI may help grammar or organization. Apply through the official Soroptimist application portal.

cells.formattedValue: Montana STEM/Healthcare Scholarship Program is for Montana residents applying in the year they graduate from a high school accredited by the Montana Board of Public Education. It requires at least a 3.25 cumulative high-school GPA, four years of college-prep math and three years of college-prep science. Students must be accepted at an eligible campus, declare a qualifying STEM or healthcare major, seek their first certificate, two-year or four-year degree, enroll in at least 12 credits each semester and begin in the fall immediately after graduation. Apply through AwardMontana by March 15 (cycle year not stated), with the seventh-semester transcript, acceptance proof and counselor-signed math/science certification. Awards are $1,000 in year one, $1,500 in years two and three and $2,000 in year four if continuing requirements are met; not every program necessarily lasts four years.

cells.formattedValue: Dr.Christine Lawther First in the Family Scholarship supports first-generation college students pursuing a four-year undergraduate degree. This is a conditional undergraduate opportunity; eligibility before beginning undergraduate study is not confirmed. The public Apply Now control links to Bold.org signup. Applicants provide a400–600-word essay about being first in their family to obtain a college degree, what they want to pursue in college, and their long-term goals. The current deadline is April1,2027. No GPA, income threshold, major restriction or renewal guarantee is established. The program does not further define first-generation status, so the interview's immediate-family attendance wording does not independently prove eligibility.

Applicants submit400–600words about advocacy in the Asian American community and their goals, and upload an image of themselves helping or a school portrait. High-school-only eligibility is not confirmed; this is a conditional undergraduate opportunity.

cells.formattedValue: Donald E. Pizzini Memorial Nurse Scholarships provide up to $2,500 for full-time or part-time accredited nursing degree or certificate study relevant to long-term care. Applicants must be US citizens or permanent residents, reside in Montana, plan to work or remain working in Montana long-term-care nursing, and be available for a qualifying interview. A 3.0 prior GPA is required, using high-school GPA for first-year students; the committee may waive it for current long-term-care professionals based on work performance and experience. Acceptance or enrollment proof, official transcripts and two non-family recommendations are required. Preference goes to current long-term-care workers or those interested in that career, and people with current or past MHCA-member-facility employment. Use the official Initial Scholarship Application PDF for applicants who have not previously received this award. Applications are due the last day of February, with awards in April for the coming academic year; the year is unstated. Enrollment and continued participation must be proved for payments; the committee may withhold/cancel funds below3.0. Recipients may reapply after their award expires; renewal is not guaranteed.

This is distinct from HPFY Make a Difference, which is already in Master.
